answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation earned, not claimed. A new identity starts with zero weight and must complete real jobs that peers verify; each verified job adds a small pulse of trust to its history, and weight grows only with diverse counterparties. A sock-puppet cluster is a closed wharf: its members trade only with each other, so their shared history forms a tight spiral with no outside attestations, which the network discounts automatically. Faking a hundred identities then costs a hundred genuine job histories, more work than the fraud is worth.
